# Routstr provider node — instructions for an operator's agent

Goal: help an operator set up a Routstr node without exposing the bootstrap admin
password or assuming that a running API is a working provider. This file is a
standalone entry point for agents without an existing checkout. The commands,
Compose file and detailed human steps live in the checked-out repository; read
`docs/provider/quickstart.md` and `docs/provider/deployment.md` after cloning.

## Who does what

The operator does exactly the items below. Everything else is the agent's job —
including DNS records, TLS, the reverse proxy, installing Docker, cloning,
checkout, `.env`, port selection, starting Compose, generating keys, dashboard
configuration that takes no secret, `check`, verification and every report. Do
not ask the operator to confirm or approve an agent step; do it and report it.

Each phase marks its operator items and ends at a gate. At a gate, stop and wait
for the operator's artifact. Report the blocker, not a fabricated success.

### Operator items (closed list)

- **O1 — Answer once, up front.** The domain or subdomain to serve
  (`https://node.example`), or "private, no domain yet"; and the payout Lightning
  address (`user@wallet.example`, `lnurl1…`, or an `https://` LNURL-pay endpoint).
  Nothing else is needed to start. Naming a domain also approves publishing the
  Nostr listing on first boot.
- **O2 — Privileged access.** When an agent step needs host root (installing
  Docker, DNS, TLS, the reverse proxy, the firewall), ask then; the operator
  enters it or grants it.
- **O3 — Provider secrets.** The operator picks and pays for the upstream
  provider, pastes its API key into Providers themselves, and decides which model
  to enable and its pricing. The agent guides and verifies; it never sees the key.
- **O4 — Bootstrap password.** Read the one-time admin password from the node logs
  in the operator's own terminal and rotate it in Settings → Admin Settings. The
  agent supplies the exact command and URL and never reads that log line.
- **O5 — Key backup.** Back up the master key and the NSEC off-host and test a
  restore (Phase 2).
- **O6 — Paid acceptance.** With model, mint, prompt and limit approved, run small
  paid non-streaming and streaming tests with the operator's own funded client
  credential — a consumer credential, not node funding and not an admin token.

### Agent must never

- Put secrets in chat, shell arguments, Git, captured logs or generated reports,
  and never ask the operator for one — the admin password, provider API keys,
  Cashu credentials, CLI tokens and the `nsec`. A credential the agent may *use*
  but not *read* is `~/.routstr/config.json` (0600), which authorises the Routstr
  CLI.
- Run bare `docker compose up`: stock `compose.yml` publishes port 8000 on all
  interfaces and starts Tor. Every Compose operation here uses
  `-f compose.node.yml`.
- Run the log command to read the bootstrap password, or paste raw Docker logs or
  admin responses into a report.
- Report a gate as passed without the operator's artifact.

## Default flow (public mode)

The default assumes the operator names a subdomain with HTTPS and a reverse proxy
forwarding to `127.0.0.1:8000`. The node then publishes its Nostr listing on first
boot, which O1 approved. If there is no public URL yet, use private mode and
publish later.

### Phase 0 — Host

**Agent**

- Open by asking O1, before touching the host:
  - Which domain or subdomain will serve this node (`https://node.example`), or do
    they want a loopback-only node with no public URL yet? A named domain still
    needs DNS, TLS and a reverse proxy forwarding to `127.0.0.1:8000`.
  - Which payout Lightning address should receive settled earnings? It is passed to
    `start` as `--ln-address` and saved in `.env`; get it now so Phase 1 needs no
    rerun.
- Confirm Docker with the Compose plugin, Python 3, available disk and durable
  storage; install what is missing (O2 if root is needed).
- Clone `https://github.com/Routstr/routstr-core.git` if there is no checkout,
  check out the tag of the latest release, and inspect the quickstart and
  deployment guide before running commands. Only if the operator asks to test the
  current development branch, use that branch and explicitly label it as
  unreviewed. Reuse an existing checkout and state; do not overwrite `.env` or
  recreate a wallet.
- For public mode, create the DNS record, TLS certificate and reverse proxy entry
  for the O1 domain (O2 if root is needed), and verify **before** starting that
  they forward that domain to `127.0.0.1:8000`. If any of that is missing, prefer
  private mode. The dashboard is protected by the node's own admin password
  (scrypt-hashed); restricting `/admin` at the proxy (IP allowlist or basic auth)
  is an optional extra layer, not a setup requirement. The operator still reads
  the one-time bootstrap password and rotates it (O4).

**Operator**

- O1: the domain (or "private") and the payout address.
- O2: root, only if the agent asks.

Gate G0 — Phases 0 and 1 need nothing beyond O1, plus O2 where root is required.

### Phase 1 — Start

**Agent**

- Check that the loopback port is free, then run (public):

```bash
python3 scripts/node_setup.py start --public-url https://node.example --ln-address user@wallet.example
```

or private (nothing published):

```bash
python3 scripts/node_setup.py start --private
```

- If another service owns port 8000, keep it untouched and pass `--port 18080`; use
  that port for `check`, the dashboard URL, the reverse proxy and later
  `ROUTSTR_NODE_PORT=18080 docker compose -f compose.node.yml …` commands.
- Report ref/version, port, reachability and model count.

`start` prepares `.env` (never clobbering existing values), starts
`compose.node.yml` (loopback only, no Tor, analytics off on first boot), waits for the local
`/v1/info` and `/v1/models`, generates the master key and Nostr identity, and — in
public mode — publishes the listing (approved by O1). It also mints a long-lived
CLI token and writes it to `~/.routstr/config.json` (0600) for the Routstr CLI;
skip that with `--no-cli-token`. If that file already points at another node,
`start` leaves it alone and creates no token (see the Routstr CLI section below).
A running API with zero models is **not configured**.

### Phase 2 — Back up

**Agent**

- Hand the operator the numbered list below, with the reveal command.
- Afterwards verify that both artifacts exist at the backup target (name, size,
  hash). Never read their contents.

**Operator** (O5)

The master key and identity exist as soon as the node boots. Back up exactly two
things, off-host and encrypted:

1. The NSEC — the node's Nostr identity key. In your own terminal:

```bash
docker compose -f compose.node.yml exec routstr /.venv/bin/python scripts/reveal_nsec.py
```

2. `routstr_secret.key` — the master key file.

Test a restore once, somewhere isolated. Keep the two together: the master key
decrypts the `nsec` stored in `keys.db`. Do not ingest the revealed `nsec` or any
logs into the agent context.

Gate G1 — "both items stored and restore tested."

### Phase 3 — Dashboard

**Agent**

- Hand the operator the dashboard address (`https://node.example/admin` in public
  mode, or `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin` over an SSH tunnel).
- After the operator acts, verify model routing, pricing, payout address, mints and
  relays through the admin API, without printing provider records or secrets.

**Operator**

- O4: read the generated password privately from
  `docker compose -f compose.node.yml logs routstr`, log in, and immediately rotate
  it in Settings → Admin Settings.
- O3: add the upstream in Providers with your own API key, enable at least one
  routable model, and review pricing, payout address, mints and relays.

Gate G2 — "password rotated, upstream added, at least one model enabled."

### Phase 4 — Verify and accept

**Agent**

- Run:

```bash
python3 scripts/node_setup.py check --public-url https://node.example
```

Require exit code 0 and a nonzero public model count (exit code 2 means the API is
running but not configured). If it fails, diagnose without printing provider
records or secrets. This proves discovery only — it is **not** a paid-inference
test.
- Verify completion, accounting, upstream serving, refund status and payout
  separately through the admin API.

**Operator**

- O6: with model, mint, prompt and limit approved, run small paid non-streaming and
  streaming inference tests with your own funded client credential (not an admin
  token).

Gate G3 — paid-inference verification, or an explicit "discovery only" outcome.

### Handoff

Report ref/version, private/public reachability, whether password rotation was
confirmed (never the password), model count, backup/restore status, paid-inference
verification status and which gates passed. "Local API ready" and "production
accepted" are separate outcomes. Never paste raw Docker logs or admin responses.

## Routstr CLI

The setup writes a long-lived admin token to `~/.routstr/config.json` (0600), so
the [Routstr CLI](https://github.com/routstr/routstr-cli) is ready to operate the
node. The agent may use that token but must never print or read it. If that file
already pointed at another node, `start` left it alone and minted no token. The
CLI only reads `$HOME/.routstr/config.json`, so re-run `start` with
`--cli-config /some/dir/.routstr/config.json` and run the CLI as
`HOME=/some/dir routstr …`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/routstr/routstr-cli.git
cd routstr-cli && bun install

routstr instruct          # canonical agent guide for this node
routstr schema            # full command tree as JSON
routstr status
routstr providers list
routstr providers add openrouter --api-key <key> --base-url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
```

The token is **full node admin**. Give each agent its own named, expiring token
and revoke it when done (**Settings → CLI Tokens**, or
`DELETE /admin/api/cli-tokens/{id}`). On a different machine, configure the CLI
with `routstr init --node-url <url> --token <token>`. Mint another token with
`docker compose -f compose.node.yml exec routstr /.venv/bin/python scripts/create_cli_token.py --name agent`.
Never paste the token, or the generated admin password, into a chat.

## Private mode (no public URL yet)

Everything above holds, except `HTTP_URL` is unset: the node is loopback-only and
publishes nothing. Administer it over an SSH tunnel, and promote it later by
setting the public **HTTP URL** in the dashboard (the listing is then published
automatically). Publication is an operator decision: ask before promoting.
